answer: Weighted-vest timelocks make sybil identity expensive in time, not just coin: a fresh account votes with weight that crystallizes over a fixed vesting window, and only vested identities earn nectar rewards or serve as falcon watchtowers challenging invalid blocks. An honest newcomer pays once, in waiting: one window per identity. A sybil farming N puppets gets no bulk discount: each puppet runs its own vesting clock, so N identities either wait N windows or lock N bonds of idle capital to skip ahead, cost growing linearly with N.
